body:
Review pass 29. First, a correction: you resumed. My pass-28 call that the session had stopped was premature - it was a 34-minute gap, not a stop. Epic 7 closed at 11:24 and Epic 8 is now claimed.

EPIC 7 CLOSED WELL. Your conclusion took both things I recommended and went further:
- equivalence margin (+/-0.005) rather than a null result
- a MISSPECIFIED arm (unmodelled AR(1)) alongside the well-specified one - that was the scope condition I flagged, and it is where the material effect actually lives
- follow-up research issue bd-01KZXVJVFCF5BG5RZSS8ZCJYJZ, which is criterion 7 satisfied with a real artifact rather than a note
- training-only kept as conservative default, all-run explicit, no CI/LD-t export while metric randomness is uncalibrated
That is a better answer than the one I handed you, and the AR(1) result is the scientifically interesting part.

NEW FINDING, bd-01KZXW5MFZGEXVJ3CMKMGBGFZX (p2), and it is partly my fault since I recommended the pinning.

test-crossnobis-known.R now uses replications <- 64L; it was 120. The pinned constants were not rescaled:
  expected_standard_errors <- c(null = 0.0058, signal = 0.0119)
Those were measured at 120. MC se scales as 1/sqrt(reps), so at 64 they should be ~1.37x larger. Measured on the exact fixture:

  reps=64  observed se: null 0.00860  signal 0.01418
           ratio observed/pinned: null 1.48  signal 1.19    (gate is 1.50)
           headroom: null 1%   signal 26%

So the variance gate passes with ONE PERCENT of margin - a different seed, BLAS or platform will trip it. And in the other direction the mean gate is now 4/1.48 = 2.7 sigma rather than the intended 4. Both wrong, same cause.

Preferred fix removes the coupling rather than patching it: pin the per-replication SD and derive the se inside the test.
  expected_sd <- c(null = 0.0635, signal = 0.1304)   # pinned se * sqrt(120)
  expected_se <- expected_sd / sqrt(replications)
Then changing replications can never invalidate the constants again.

ONE MORE FOR EPIC 9: the 500-replication study lives in benchmarks/run-learned-metric-policy-validation.R, not the test suite. Reasonable for a slow study, but it means the evidence behind the Epic 7 conclusion is not run by test_local() or R CMD check - same structural situation as the scale gates. If Epic 9 certifies the policy conclusion it should say the study is a benchmark artifact and when it was last run. Noted there.
